# The Weight of Honor
## Scripture
"Let love be genuine. Abhor what is evil; hold fast to what is good. Love one another with brotherly affection. Outdo one another in showing honor." – Romans 12:9-10

## Reflection
Men, we live in a culture that tells us to look out for number one, to climb the ladder, and to keep score. But Paul calls us to something radically different: outdo one another in showing honor. That means your competitive drive—the one God gave you—should be aimed at loving your brothers, your wife, your kids, and even your enemies *more* fiercely than they love you. Don't just tolerate them; chase them down with respect and genuine affection. This is not weakness; it's the strength of a warrior who has nothing to prove. When you lay down your ego and pick up the towel of service, you reflect Christ, who honored us by dying for us. Your physical strength will fade, but the legacy of honor you build will echo into eternity. Be the man who fights to lift others up, not to push them down.

## Daily Challenge
Before your workout, text one brother and tell him one specific way he's sharpened you. Then, during your workout, do your final set of reps "for him" as a prayer of thanks.
